newsitem.title: USA: Levitz, others agree to $10 mln Calif. settlement.
newsitem.headline: Levitz, others agree to $10 mln Calif. settlement.

text.p: Levitz Furniture Inc and other defendants will pay $10 million to settle a lawsuit that claimed they illegally sold insurance to unwitting furniture customers, California officials said Tuesday.

California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush said he and four California district attorneys filed a civil complaint Monday claiming Pennsylvania furniture retailer Levitz and several co-defendants unlawfully sold various kinds of insurance to customers who opened revolving credit accounts to finance furniture purchases.

Levitz's co-defendants in the litigation include General Electric Co's GE Capital Corp, American Bankers Insurance Co (ABIG) and American Bankers Life Assurance Co of Florida. ABIG was the underwriter of the credit insurance. GE Capital arranged and placed the credit insurance and also bought the revolving accounts, the complaint said.

According to the complaint, the defendants' practices resulted in many Levitz customers buying a package of optional credit insurance products -- including credit life, disability, unemployment and property insurance -- without knowing they had done so.
All defendants, without admitting wrongdoing, entered into a stipulated final judgment Monday that concluded the litigation.
The judgment provides for a restitution of up to $4.1 million to unwitting customers who bought the additional insurance between January 1993 and February of this year.
The judgment also requires Levitz to pay a civil penalty of $2 million and requires all defendants to reimburse the district attorneys and the Department of Insurance $2.025 million.
San Mateo County District Attorney Jim Fox called the settlement the second-largest of its type ever in the state.
Officials at Levitz were not immediately available to comment on the settlement.
